title: Distinguish normal exit from signal termination
goal: Report a native worker’s exit status without treating a POSIX signal as an ordinary application exit code.

selectionNotes: SIGTERM can be ignored; impose a bounded stop policy. Windows has no POSIX signal result. macOS execution is unverified.
Not tested: macOS execution: no Mac environment. Excluded under PIN-699; recorded Windows/Linux results remain separate.

prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0. Include the imports stated in the recipe.
constraints: Signal is a request, not a guarantee of termination: a Unix application can handle or ignore SIGTERM. A production stop policy should impose a grace period, then force termination when its own contract allows it. false can indicate an exit race; still collect status. Permissions, an invalid/closed handle and a process exiting between lookup and signalling need their own error handling. The test’s default-signal worker terminates, and Linux preserves SIGTERM separately from normal exit 7. Windows execution checks Signal=null. macOS uses the guarded POSIX route but has no native execution proof. SafeProcessHandle offers the equivalent Signal/wait primitives without the Process component.
